Subject: Renewal + Expansion: Pricing step-ups & blended rates (post-call recap)

Hey Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + next steps so we’re aligned: 

What we covered:
- Renewal: 12-month renewal starting 2026-07-01 for current routes/models (same product mix)
- Expansion: add 3 new routes for clinical summarization and a higher-throughput model for batch inference
- Volume profile: you expect a baseline of ~120M tokens/month with step-ups to 250M by Q4; see attached schedule for month-by-month forecast.
- Budget: target blended unit economics in the range of $700–$900 per 1M tokens for the expanded footprint (finance will confirm).

Open items / next steps we agreed:
1) Alex to confirm final monthly token projection and any seasonality by Friday 2026-06-05 (you mentioned finance needs to sign off).
2) Redwood to provide a pricing proposal that includes: a) volume step-up tiers, b) blended rates across models/routes, and c) PO/contract timeline.
3) If budget requires, we’ll propose a blended pricing option with committed minimums + overage pricing.

I’ve attached the volume schedule you sketched out during the call — I filled in a couple of assumptions (highlighted). If anything there is off, flag it and I’ll update.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Marissa

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and for filling in the assumptions. Finance reviewed overnight and provided an initial target budget range for the expanded deployment:

- Confirmed baseline: 120M tokens/month (May-Jun)
- Expected step-ups: 170M (Jul), 200M (Aug), 250M (Sep onward)
- Target blended cost: $750/1M tokens +/- $100 (they asked for elasticity on model mix)
- Contract note: procurement prefers a single renewal effective date (2026-07-01) and wants any credits applied at renewal

We’re comfortable moving forward with a proposal. Can you show a scenario with a blended rate assuming 60% standard gen model usage, 30% summarization route (higher cost), 10% embeddings/rerank?

Also, procurement asked whether adding the new high-throughput model would change the unit economics materially — they want a worst-case blended rate and a best-case with quantization/spotting.

If you can get that to us early next week, we’ll review with finance and circle back.

—Alex

Subject: Re: Renewal + Expansion: Pricing step-ups & blended rates (proposal attached)

Hi Alex —

Appended a short proposal with two scenarios: Committed Tiers (preferred) and a Blended/Elastic option. Key highlights: 

Scenario A — Committed Tiers (recommended):
- 0–150M: $950 / 1M tokens
- 150–220M: $825 / 1M tokens
- 220M+: $700 / 1M tokens
- Commitment: 12 months, quarterly true-ups, month-to-month overage at $1,100 / 1M tokens

Scenario B — Blended/Elastic (for procurement flexibility):
- Blend price (weighted across routes): $760 / 1M tokens (based on 60/30/10 split, see calc)
- Adds a CPI-style cap: worst-case blended $900 / 1M, best-case $650/1M with quantization/spot on dedicated capacity

I attached the detailed blended-rate calculation (blended_rate_calc.csv) and a short PDF proposal (redwood_pricing_proposal_v2.pdf). We also called out assumptions for model mix, quantization possibility, and rollout timing.

Questions for you: 
- Does procurement require any specific invoicing cadence (monthly vs. quarterly)?
- Would you like the high-throughput model on the same contract, or scoped as an add-on with its own minimums?

If both answers are yes, we can draft an amendment for the renewal that includes the new routes and blended pricing.

Thanks — I’ll let Lukas add a note on blended math and CS handover.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: blended_rate_calc.csv, redwood_pricing_proposal_v2.pdf

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + Expansion: Pricing step-ups & blended rates (blended math)

Alex —

Quick breakdown of the blended math we used (pulled from blended_rate_calc.csv):
- Assumptions: 60% standard gen model @ $700/1M (post-commit tier), 30% summarization route @ $1,400/1M, 10% embeddings @ $300/1M
- Weighted blended = 0.6*700 + 0.3*1400 + 0.1*300 = $760 / 1M tokens
- If 20% of gen traffic can shift to a quantized variant we expect best-case blended ~ $650 / 1M; worst-case (no quantization, higher summarization usage) ~ $900 / 1M

Operational notes (for CS/procurement):
- We recommend locking in the committed tiers on the renewal for predictability and applying blended pricing for any additional ad-hoc routes during the term.
- For the new high-throughput model: recommend add-on with a 3-month ramp minimum or include it as part of the tier if ACME commits to >=50M extra tokens/month.

Ethan, I’ll hand this over to you for implementation plan and SLA ramp checklist.

—Lukas
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
